question: Is NESO national day-ahead demand the same target scope as the course daily demand?
course_target: Repaired Elexon demand/outturn/summary recordTypeVD; equal-duration UTC-day mean. Missing/bad slots reconstructed from calibrated NESO TSD, not ND.
neso_forecast_target: National Demand: operational GB generation requirement, excluding station load, pumped-storage pumping and interconnector exports. Forecasts at cardinal points, not daily time-weighted mean.
project_boundary: Official brief calls datasets a constructed client energy system; actual client is hypothetical, not literally allGB demand. Teacher uses aggregate UK generation/demand and ignores grid routing.
geographical_relation: Broad GB-system scale in underlying public data; not a verified customer-specific forecast.
exact_equivalence: Not established; do not label NESO ND forecast an official same-definition forecast of courseVD.

diagnostic.filter: 288VD API output records, all>=10000MW; no imputedVD values used in comparison

inference: Observed course-sourceVD is much closer to NESOTSD than ND. This supports a broader system-demand interpretation but does not by itself proveVD=TSD or uniquely explain the remaining241MW average difference.
modelling_implication: Valid as an as-of external predictor of courseVD if publication cutoff holds; empirical improvement is transferable information gain, not evidence our model beats NESO on its own exact target.
missing_control: NESO-only calibrated mapping to courseVD has not been isolated as a baseline.

sources.verified: System demand summary(FUELINST), a downsampled visualisation summary.
Underlying operational generation data concerns GreatBritain.
Official ND/TSD definitions and exclusions; ND maps toINDO and national forecast, TSD toITSDO and transmission forecast.
Page2 constructed client system; not detailed Scottish transmission picture.
Around01:09-01:17 UKaggregate simplifying assumption; provided transcript, not independently audio-verified.
